backend.title: Backend
backend.description: Who writes the message. Claude Code and Codex use the CLI you are signed in to (the same one the IDE's agents use) and need its process permission; the APIs need a key under Settings › Plugins; local is any OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio). Test it with the button below.

claudeModel.title: Model
claudeModel.description: Passed as --model (haiku, sonnet, opus or a full model id). Empty: the CLI's default. Claude Code runs without tools, MCP servers and the project's .claude settings.

codexModel.title: Model
codexModel.description: Passed as --model. Empty: Codex's built-in default (your ~/.codex/config.toml is not read, so its model and reasoning settings do not apply).

anthropicModel.title: Model
anthropicModel.description: claude-haiku-5-5 is fast and cheap; claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-opus-5-5 for harder diffs. The API key goes in Settings › Plugins: select AI Commit Message in the list, then Secrets.

anthropicEffort.title: Effort
anthropicEffort.description: How much the model thinks first. default: the model's own default (and for models without effort).

openaiModel.title: Model
openaiModel.description: The API key goes in Settings › Plugins: select AI Commit Message in the list, then Secrets.

localUrl.title: Chat completions URL
localUrl.description: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM. localhost and 127.0.0.1 need their permission (net:localhost, net:127.0.0.1); any other host must use https:// and is allowed once, when the IDE asks (net:ask).
